en: Ati-Atihan dancers drink water to maintain thermoregulation and prevent heatstroke while dancing under the hot Kalibo sun.
The Ifugao people build stone-walled rice terraces to prevent soil erosion and landslides during heavy rains in the Cordilleras.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in rural areas without electricity.
PHIVOLCS teaches students to duck, cover, and hold during earthquakes because the Philippines sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire.
National hero Jose Rizal studied ophthalmology in Europe to learn how to cure his mother’s growing eye cataracts.
Exercising the constitutional right to health involves getting scientifically formulated vaccines at barangay centers to build immunity against diseases.
The Department of Health promotes lagundi leaves as a scientifically proven traditional herbal medicine to relieve coughs and asthma.
Barangay officials enforce evacuations during typhoons because meteorological science shows storm surges can fatally flood low-lying coastal communities.
The Philippine Red Cross uses scientific blood typing to ensure bayanihan-driven voluntary donations safely match donors with patients.
Farmers must wash their hands with soap after handling carabaos to prevent contracting zoonotic diseases like leptospirosis.
The Aeta indigenous people use their deep botanical knowledge to identify safe, edible wild plants and avoid toxic ones.
Passengers must hold jeepney handrails to counteract inertia and avoid falling when the culturally iconic vehicle suddenly brakes.
